messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout (model v12) is showing elevated streaming tail latency in eu-west-1. p95 ~ 210ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~ 1.8s -> 4.6s. Error rate unchanged. Auto-page to oncall.
marie.sre: oncall here, grabbing details. Which pool did traffic hit? :eyes:
ajay.platform: looks like traffic shift routed ~18% to canary pool 'dedicated-v12-eu' at 12:11 UTC. Batcher queue depth spiked. Logs show KV cache refresh storms.
emily-eng: seeing a lot of stalled multiplex streams on the canary hosts. stack traces show long waits in grpc write loop. Could be backpressure from encoder warmups.
marie.sre: any customer impact? Dana, can you check the top routes? @dana-support
dana-support: looking at support metrics — a handful of users in EU reported slow streaming responses but no 5xx. We have one customer (acme-inc) latency alert in their app, raising a ticket.
marie.sre: ok escalate to postmortem if rollback needed. First priority: prevent broader impact. Suggested mitigations: 1) throttle canary traffic back to 0-1% 2) fallback to v11 for streaming 3) increase batcher threads.
ajay.platform: I can flip traffic routing. Do we want immediate rollback or gradual traffic cut? If we cut to 0-1% now we avoid more users seeing high p99.
emily-eng: rollback recommended for streaming endpoints. The root cause looks like encoder cold-starts + an interaction with the continuous batching logic that increases per-request latency when encoder queue is saturated.
marie.sre: do it. @ajay.platform please shift canary to 0% and route to v11 for streaming. Keep canary on for non-streaming, if safe.
ajay.platform: starting traffic shift now. executing:
```
deployctl route set canary dedicated-v12-eu --percent 0 --routes streaming
deployctl route set default dedicated-v11-eu --percent 100 --routes streaming
```
deploy-bot: deployctl: traffic change submitted by ajay.platform. change id: tc-223344-78. Started at 12:24:08 UTC.
emily-eng: also patching a short-term change to batcher config to increase max inflight per-worker from 64 -> 128 on canary nodes, in case we toggle back.
marie.sre: good. ajay, confirm when traffic finished shifting.
ajay.platform: route change completed. Canary streaming traffic ~0.6% (routing propagation). Will watch.
incident-bot: Monitor: p99 streaming latency in eu-west-1 reduced from 4.6s -> 1.1s within 45s of traffic shift. p95 stabilized ~230ms.
dana-support: update: acme-inc noticing improvement. Their alert cleared. They still had a single degraded session but overall OK now.
emily-eng: capturing logs from the problematic canary hosts: frequent logs like
```
WARN encoder: cold-start for shard=3, encoded_tokens=0, wait=3120ms
WARN batcher: inflight=102, queue_len=78, flush_time=520ms
```
These suggest encoder warmups + batcher queue saturation causing head-of-line blocking for streaming frames.
marie.sre: any evidence of kv locks or redis pressure?
ajay.platform: redis metrics show a spike in hmget latency coincident with canary traffic ramp — avg hmget 8ms -> 45ms on the canary subset. Could be cache churn from new model embedding keys.
emily-eng: that plus encoder cold starts makes sense: more requests hitting cold KV entries -> longer lookup -> longer encoder queue -> backpressure to grpc write.
marie.sre: next steps: 1) keep canary streaming at 0-1% until we identify fixes. 2) run a targeted warmup for encoder on canary hosts and pre-populate KV entries. 3) schedule a quick rollback policy update so future rollouts ramp slower for streaming routes.
ajay.platform: filed rollback policy change MR: https://git.internal/repo/mr/4521 (slower ramp + canary health gate includes p99 streaming < 800ms). Will fast-track review.
emily-eng: I'll prepare a warmup job to run across canary hosts (preload encoder and prime KV). Running a one-off job now.
marie.sre: thanks. Dana, advise ops and customer success that we rolled streaming back and are doing mitigations; we can offer proactive outreach to customers that saw degradation.
dana-support: will post update in support ticket for acme-inc and add a proactive note to impacted customers. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: NOTE: Oncall handoff scheduled in 2h. marie.sre will hand to next oncall unless needed.
marie.sre: quick timeline notes for postmortem: incident detected 12:11 UTC (automated canary ramp), mitigation (traffic rollback) at 12:24 UTC, p99 improved by 12:25 UTC. Keeping this thread for root cause and follow-ups.
emily-eng: after warmup job, I'll run a controlled ramp to 5% with probing load to validate fix. Will post experiment results here.
ajay.platform: monitoring metrics to watch: batcher inflight, encoder latency, redis hmget p50/p99, grpc send queue length. I'll add dashboards.
marie.sre: one more ask — add a dashboard alert that triggers if canary p99 > 1s within 30s of ramping >5% traffic for streaming routes. Otherwise we'll miss this pattern.
ajay.platform: creating alert now. alert rule id: a-223344-7. ETA 10m.
dana-support: customer comms draft: "We briefly observed higher-than-expected streaming latency during a canary rollout. We rolled back streaming traffic to previous version and are investigating root cause. No data loss reported." Will share draft for legal review.
marie.sre: thanks all. We'll leave this thread open. If any regression or stuck rollback happens, page immediately. :wave:
